clue.text: Recalled a celebration mass in Spanish port

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration
M is the standard abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: Someone remembers a festive mass held in a Spanish harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' turns the whole run A + GALA + M (AGALAM) back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaga is a port city on Spain's Costa del Sol.

clue.text: New York opera's suppressing old time pieces of music

indicators.note: suppressing is read as holding down inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the Met is New York's Metropolitan Opera; the possessive gives the final S

explanation.surface: A New York opera house keeps an old timepiece out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old time pieces' looks like clocks; O and T go inside METS.
explanation.definitionFit: Motets are short choral compositions, usually sacred, so they are pieces of music.

clue.text: Country exiling an 80s singer

indicators.note: exiling means sending away, so these letters are removed from the country

parts.note: Lebanon is a Middle Eastern country

explanation.surface: A nation banishes a pop star from the 1980s.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking AN out of LEBANON leaves LEBON: Simon Le Bon, singer of the 1980s band Duran Duran.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon Le Bon fronted Duran Duran, one of the biggest pop acts of the 1980s.

clue.text: Travels to Brest as arranged following journey across Channel at last

indicators.note: following says the rearranged letters come after the other piece
across means spanning, so the journey word straddles the letter

parts.note: to go is to make a journey

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word Channel
as arranged signals the letters of to Brest are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone takes a planned trip to Brest after crossing the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' suggests the English Channel crossing, but only its last letter is used. 'as arranged' gives BETROTS, 'across' puts L inside the journey word, and 'following' sets the anagram last.
explanation.definitionFit: To globetrot is to travel widely around the world, so a person who does so travels.

clue.text: Urgent job once grapes are picked?

definitions.meaning: after the harvest grapes are squeezed for their juice in winemaking

explanation.definitionFit: Something urgent is pressing, and squeezing harvested grapes for wine is the pressing.

clue.text: Two causes of disaster in the main for a musician

definitions.text: Two causes of disaster in the main
definitions.meaning: the main is the sea, where ships are wrecked on a rock or swamped by a great wave called a roller
a performer of the 1950s style of popular music

explanation.definitionFit: A rock-and-roll performer is a musician, and read as two words the phrase names a reef and a big wave, both maritime hazards.

clue.text: Twist a lot

definitions.meaning: to turn or swing round sharply

explanation.definitionFit: Slew means both to swing round and, informally, a great many.

clue.text: I get close to home showing determination

parts.note: near means close to
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Someone moves nearer their house with resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in earnest means doing it seriously and with resolve.

clue.text: Enjoy friendly relations? Piffle

definitions.meaning: to be on good terms with someone
an exclamation of disbelief, like saying nonsense

explanation.definitionFit: People on good terms get along, and 'get along with you!' is a scoffing retort meaning nonsense.

clue.text: Smoke rings forbidden

parts.note: a tab is slang for a cigarette
the letter O is ring-shaped, so two rings give two Os

explanation.surface: Smoke rings are not allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: TAB is northern British slang for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is prohibited by custom.

clue.text: In most of island people accepted wage rise

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so one piece goes inside the other
most of means the final letter of the island is dropped

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island
men means people

explanation.surface: On most of an island, workers agreed to a pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the island's final E, and 'accepted' takes the people inside what remains; IN is the clue's own first word.
explanation.definitionFit: An increment is a regular step up in salary on a pay scale.

clue.text: Maybe how I've got trainer repaired

indicators.note: repaired suggests something put back together differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's running shoe has been mended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' shows the definition is by example: 'how' is one such word.
explanation.definitionFit: How is a question word, an example of the grammatical class used to ask questions.

clue.text: In Natal get lost, deviating from course

indicators.note: lost suggests letters wandering out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller loses their way in Natal, straying off route.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangential means going off at a tangent, diverging from the main line.

clue.text: Test shortened for a learner

indicators.note: shortened means a letter is cut from the word for

parts.note: L is the learner plate letter on British cars

explanation.surface: An examination is cut down to suit a novice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' takes F off FOR, leaving OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken examination, as in a language exam, is a test.

clue.text: Guess I'm stuck in English Channel

indicators.note: stuck in means placed inside another word

parts.note: a TV or radio channel is a station

explanation.surface: A traveller supposes they are stranded in the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' looks like the sea; it is a broadcasting station.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimation is a rough calculation or judgement, a guess.

clue.text: Obtain most offensive German article about radical writer

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the letter

parts.note: to get is to obtain
R is an abbreviation for radical
rudest means most offensive
ein is the German indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone fetches a rude German piece about an extremist author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside GET to give GERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Gertrude Stein was an American author and poet of the modernist era.

clue.text: Soldier meets new friend at top watering hole

parts.note: GI is a US soldier
a pal is a friend
ace means first-rate, at the top

explanation.surface: A soldier meets a fresh friend at a top bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin palace is a British term for a showy, gaudy Victorian pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A watering hole is slang for a pub, and a gin palace is a flashy pub.

clue.text: Noble precursor of Labour's ISA?

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, the party in power before Labour
a TESSA was the Conservative tax-free savings account that Labour's ISA replaced in 1999

explanation.surface: An aristocrat is asked what came before a government savings scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: British savings accounts: TESSA, introduced by the Conservatives, was replaced by the Individual Savings Account under Labour.
explanation.definitionFit: A contessa is an Italian countess, a noblewoman.

clue.text: Various irons too light for one interested in birdies?

indicators.note: various suggests a mixture, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer finds a set of clubs is too light.
explanation.walkthrough: Golf misleads: irons are clubs and a birdie is a score, but the definition means real birds.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornithologist studies birds, playfully called birdies.

clue.text: Short, thickset and fox-y?

definitions.meaning: to fox is to baffle, so this means baffling

explanation.definitionFit: A squat person is stumpy, and since to stump means to baffle, stumpy jokily means baffling.

clue.text: Duck leaves lake

parts.note: tea is the dried leaves for brewing

explanation.surface: A duck flies away from a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb but is a noun, tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The teal is a small freshwater duck.

clue.text: Member of Oasis taking part in pop congress?

indicators.note: taking part in means going inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: pop is a word for father, a parent
Liam Gallagher was a member of the band Oasis

explanation.surface: A Britpop band member joins a pop music conference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop' looks like music; it is a father.
explanation.definitionFit: A congress is a national legislative assembly, the same kind of body as a parliament.

clue.text: Frenchman turned green before end of voyage

indicators.note: turned means turned around, so the word for green is read backwards

parts.note: lime is a shade of green

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of voyage

explanation.surface: A Frenchman went pale green before the trip was over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reads LIME backwards as EMIL; the last letter of voyage then adds E.
explanation.definitionFit: Emile is a French male first name.

clue.text: Rear female animal

definitions.meaning: a female deer, especially red deer

explanation.definitionFit: Hind legs are at the back, and a female red deer is called a hind.

clue.text: 1'I'll treat lawn, one with nasty mark left by wild fire

indicators.note: left by means placed to the left of, so this pair comes first

parts.note: a scar is a mark left by a wound
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of fire run riot and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener's tool speaks about mending a lawn scorched by a wildfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges FIRE into FIER; 'left by' puts SCAR and I first.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarifier is a garden tool that rakes moss and thatch out of lawns.

clue.text: African dictator introducing order, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: introducing means leading in, so this piece comes before the other

parts.note: Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A tyrant brings in a new regime, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is an expression particular to a language, a turn of phrase.

clue.text: A river goes through city, one in Scotland

indicators.note: goes through means passing inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Bern is the capital of Switzerland
the Dee is a river in Scotland and Wales

explanation.surface: A river flows through a Scottish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'city' is BERN in the wordplay; 'one in Scotland' is the definition, another city.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is a city on Scotland's north-east coast.

clue.text: Animated character full of cold

definitions.meaning: one of the seven dwarfs in Disney's Snow White cartoon
having a cold that makes you keep sneezing

explanation.definitionFit: Sneezy is a dwarf in Disney's Snow White, and someone with a heavy cold is sneezy.
